articles.headline: 15 killed as truck runs into devotees near M.P. temple
articles.blurb: Fifteen people were killed and more than 40 injured after a truck laden with paddy ploughed through barricades into devotees near the Sheetla Mata temple in Gwalior around 1.30 a.m. on Sunday. CM Mohan Yadav ordered a probe, transferred the City SP, suspended eight personnel, and announced ex gratia of ₹4 lakh to kin of the deceased, ₹2 lakh for the critically injured and ₹50,000 for others; PM Narendra Modi announced ₹2 lakh per deceased and ₹50,000 per injured from the PMNRF, and the driver and owner were arrested from Dholpur.

articles.headline: Toll in Kolkata pandal stampede rises to 19
articles.blurb: The death toll in Saturday’s stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbajanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata rose to 19 on Sunday, with four children and 11 women among the dead; seven people including the puja committee secretary and vice-president were arrested. Police filed a suo motu case under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita; the West Bengal government announced ₹25 lakh compensation to kin of the deceased as CM Suvendu Adhikari ordered crowd-management steps for the rest of the festival.

articles.headline: Kambala debuts at Mysuru Dasara; 150 pairs of buffaloes compete
articles.blurb: Kambala made its Mysuru Dasara debut on Sunday as Urban Development Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah flagged off the two-day buffalo race at Sathagalli near VTU, featuring 150 pairs. Dr. Yathindra said bringing a pair to Mysuru costs around ₹5 lakh; Puttur MLA Ashok Rai credited CM D.K. Shivakumar and said the sport draws an estimated 30 lakh to 40 lakh spectators across Karnataka.

articles.headline: Use of mobile phones in speaker mode on trains to attract ₹5,000 fine
articles.blurb: Invoking Section 145 (2)(a) of the Railways Act as amended through the Jan Vishwas Act, Southern Railway said nuisance from speaker-mode audio or loud talking can lead to removal and a ₹1,000 fine, rising to six months’ simple imprisonment and/or ₹5,000 if the nuisance continues after warning; divisions were told to make regular announcements and ticket examiners may impose penalties.

articles.headline: State mandates app-based night-time attendance for taluk and PHC doctors
articles.blurb: From November 1, doctors at taluk hospitals and PHCs must record post-9 p.m. presence via the geo-fenced Kartavya app; contract and outsourced staff must register by November 25 and mark attendance only through it from December 1, with salaries and agency bills linked to reports from January 1, 2027, under an order by Principal Secretary Harsh Gupta.

articles.headline: 'Bring citizen services online, under Sakala'
articles.blurb: Guidelines approved by CM D.K. Shivakumar make it mandatory to bring licences, certificates and other services online under Sakala, with Aadhaar as default verification, DigiLocker storage, Kutumba updates, OCR PDF uploads and QR-coded EDCS templates; departments must offer seating, water, tokens and multi-year renewals where fees alone apply.

articles.headline: Priest, accused of sexually harassing minor boys, held
articles.blurb: Mangaluru police arrested St. Vincent Ferrer Church priest Siprian Pinto for alleged aggravated sexual assault on five 14-year-olds; a victim’s complaint of October 15 cites incidents from August 14, and four friends said they faced similar conduct after the group approached the Mangaluru Bishop. The case is registered under POCSO Sections 8 and 9 and BNS Section 75(2).

articles.headline: Holding 'Pili Parba' helps preserve native culture: MP
articles.blurb: Dakshina Kannada MP Captain Brijesh Chowta inaugurated Kudla Samskritika Prathistana’s fifth annual Pili Parba at Nehru Maidan, with 11 teams performing 20 minutes each before a 6,000-capacity gallery; top three teams get ₹5 lakh, ₹3 lakh and ₹2 lakh plus ₹50,000 participation fee per team.

articles.headline: Senior Pili Veshadahari felicitated
articles.blurb: 81-year-old Gangadhar Devadiga Kadri (‘Pili Annu’) received the Karnataka Tulu Sahitya Academy Chavadi Tammana award on Sunday; Academy president Taranath Gatty cited his contribution to Pili Nalike, and MUDA chairman Santosh Kumar Shetty presented the honour.

articles.headline: Tiranga March held in Bengaluru
articles.blurb: Civil society groups carried the national flag from the Military Memorial to the Quit India Movement Memorial via the Chief Electoral Officer’s office on Sunday in solidarity with those arrested in Delhi for attempting to hoist the flag earlier in the week.

articles.headline: 'Chorus of the Coast' aboard cruise boat offers distinctive experience
articles.blurb: Indie Sound Trail and Art Kanara Trust hosted ‘Chorus of the Coast – The Homecoming Show’ aboard Abbakka Queen on the Phalguni River with 150-plus participants, contemporary music, The Floating Archive exhibition and Tulu-script stage design tied to World Tulu Script Day on October 10.

articles.headline: Woman's private photos leaked on porn websites
articles.blurb: A 28-year-old Indiranagar woman filed a complaint with East Division Cyber Crime police after intimate photos and videos she shared with a male friend allegedly appeared on porn sites following a suspected account hack.

articles.headline: Over 4,000 runners participate in Mangaluru Dasara Marathon
articles.blurb: Over 4,000 runners took part in the fourth Kudroli Gokarnanatha Temple Dasara Marathon on Sunday in 21K, 10K, 5K and 3K categories starting from the temple; the first run began at 6 a.m. after a 30-minute delay, and runners reported short water supply along routes despite police and KMC medical support.

articles.headline: Railways to operate special train on Oct. 20, 21
articles.blurb: Southern Railway will run Train 06155 Thiruvananthapuram North–Mangaluru Junction special leaving TVCN at 7.40 p.m. on October 20 and arriving MAJN at 9 a.m. on October 21, and return 06156 leaving MAJN at 10.15 a.m. on October 21, halting at Kasaragod, Kannur, Kozhikode and other stations with AC and sleeper coaches.

articles.headline: 690 pending applications related to birth, death certificates disposed of
articles.blurb: MCC disposed of 690 birth and death certificate applications in a October 14–17 drive after officials returned from Special Intensive Revision duty; Commissioner Rahul Rathnam Pandey said 217 people collected certificates by appointment and others may collect from the MCC cell at the head office.

articles.headline: GSI to organise special drive to collect e-waste from October 21 to 23
articles.blurb: GSI Marine and Coastal Survey Division, Mangaluru, will collect e-waste with 4R Recyclers at Pandeshwar from October 21 to 23, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., accepting computers, phones, appliances and other electronic waste with on-the-spot payment at applicable rates.

articles.headline: First Jamboo Savari rehearsal held at Mysuru palace
articles.blurb: Mysuru palace held the first Jamboo Savari rehearsal on Sunday including the flower-shower ritual on Goddess Chamundeshwari in the golden howdah; Police Commissioner Seema Latkar said it was to synchronise arrangements ahead of the October 21 Dasara finale.

articles.headline: Forest Department creating hurdles in implementing KUSUM-C scheme for farmers, MP complains to Shivakumar
articles.blurb: Udupi-Chikkamagaluru MP Kota Srinivas Poojary told CM D.K. Shivakumar that delay clearing acacia on 13, 7.5 and 10 acres in Byndoor, Brahmavara and Kapu taluks is holding up a ₹22 crore KUSUM-C solar project and risking withdrawal of 30% Central grant.

articles.headline: Dharwad Dasara procession to be taken out tomorrow
articles.blurb: Dharwad’s annual Dasara Jamboo Savari will be held on Tuesday from Eshwar Temple, Gandhinagar, starting with worship at Bandemma Temple and elephant Rupavathi leading the howdah procession.

articles.headline: West Bengal native detained in Kalaburagi for suspected LeT links
articles.blurb: Mumtaz-ul-Malik of West Bengal was detained in Kalaburagi over suspected Lashkar-e-Taiba-linked social media contact while working at a Saraf Bazaar jewellery workshop; Home Minister Priyank Kharge said employers should conduct background checks and promised post-festival SOP meetings with industry.

articles.headline: State extends online RTI filing to all service centres
articles.blurb: Physical RTI applications must be registered on the online portal within two days under Sakala, with compensation if delayed; filing is extended to Bengaluru One, Karnataka One and Grama One centres, and employee salary, leave and NOC requests also get fixed Sakala timelines.

articles.headline: Penalties revised
articles.blurb: The Karnataka Sakala Services (Amendment) Act, 2026 sets official delay penalties from ₹20 per day (first 1–5 days, cap ₹100) up to ₹100 per day for days 21–25 (max ₹1,500), plus up to ₹1,500 for deficient service, and ₹1,500 fines on citizens for false malicious complaints.

articles.headline: HDK cannot tolerate a Dalit like me making political progress: Priyank
articles.blurb: Home Minister Priyank Kharge accused H.D. Kumaraswamy of targeting him over KPSC and sting-operation issues and said the JD(S) leader could not tolerate a Dalit’s political progress; he defended police investigation of JD(S) activists.

articles.headline: Congress will have to pay price for misrule, says Kumaraswamy
articles.blurb: Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy said a JD(S)-BJP coalition would take power in Karnataka in 2028, demanded action on the alleged sting operation, and accused the Congress government of being servile to its architect while questioning Siddaramaiah’s silence.

articles.headline: Will CM attend Pili Nalike?
articles.blurb: Corridors of Power notes Mithun Rai has invited CM D.K. Shivakumar to a Mangaluru Pili Nalike on October 20 after Shivakumar inaugurated Dasara in Mangaluru and Udupi on October 15; Rai faced Congress show-cause notices last year for projecting Shivakumar as future CM.

articles.headline: Sub-sect unity
articles.blurb: At a Belagavi Basava Jayanti Samiti rally for Minister Laxman Savadi, former MP Ramesh Katti said Lingayat MLAs had fallen from over 90 under S. Nijalingappa to about 45–50 today and urged unity against divisive efforts including JLM’s separate-religion push.

articles.headline: On Cong.-CJP links
articles.blurb: CM D.K. Shivakumar says Congress protests on SIR are independent of the Cockroach Janta Party, while IT Minister Priyank Kharge told Bengaluru youth the Congress and CJP were ‘all the same’ in a manner of speaking.

articles.headline: BYV: Sting operations have shifted to Vidhana Soudha
articles.blurb: BJP president B.Y. Vijayendra said fake sting videos now originate from Vidhana Soudha, claimed dissidence against CM Shivakumar, challenged a KPSC scam inquiry, and accused Congress of funding CJP chaos while campaigning in Hubballi for Legislative Council polls.

articles.headline: Ration card e-KYC deadline extended to November 10
articles.blurb: The Food Department extended ration-card e-KYC to November 10 for beneficiaries who verified over a year ago or more than five years ago, completable via Anna Seva app or fair price shops, with the app available nationwide for migrants.

articles.headline: YSRCP to skip Punganur civic body polls
articles.blurb: YSRCP will skip Punganur municipality polls citing lack of transparency and security after October 16 nomination-day clashes; the party won all 31 wards unanimously in 2021 and MLA Peddireddi Ramachandra Reddy retained the seat in 2024 by 6,538 votes.

articles.headline: Telangana seeks 100% MSP procurement amid drought
articles.blurb: Agriculture Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao told a virtual meeting with Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan that drought affects 315 of 621 mandals and sought 100% MSP procurement of maize and jowar, lifting the 25% cap, and khet bachao abhiyan from October 22 to 30.

articles.headline: Heavy rain expected in many dists. in the next 24 hours
articles.blurb: IMD forecast heavy rain with lightning and 40–50 kmph gusts in Chennai, Tiruchi, Coimbatore, Nilgiris and many Tamil Nadu districts and Puducherry as northeast monsoon stays active, with a low-pressure area forming over the southwest Arabian Sea.

articles.headline: Truck with chemicals catches fire in Bengaluru; traffic hit
articles.blurb: A chemical-solvent truck caught fire on NICE Road on Sunday after a tyre burst, halting Dasara-holiday traffic for hours; the driver and assistant escaped with minor injuries from the four-tank vehicle.

articles.headline: Hubballi Chalo padayatra likely to temporarily halt today
articles.blurb: Sugarcane farmers may pause the Hubballi Chalo march on Monday before resuming after the October 23 Samyukta Kisan Morcha Delhi rally; CM Shivakumar offered a post-festival meeting and to consider a ₹4,000-per-tonne State Advised Price.

articles.headline: Keralam govt. revokes bakery's licence to sell hortiwine after row
articles.blurb: The UDF government revoked a Chalakudy bakery’s licence to sell 15%-proof hortiwine from the Beverages Corporation warehouse after CM V.D. Satheesan flagged an unconsulted Excise order; Excise Minister M. Liju sought a report from the Commissioner.

articles.headline: H.D. Kumaraswamy says his party stands with sugarcane growers
articles.blurb: H.D. Kumaraswamy said he would take cane growers’ demands to Union Minister Pralhad Joshi, noted a Central committee is examining the issue, and criticised CM Shivakumar for deferring relief talks until after Dasara.

articles.headline: DKS seeks PM's appointment to discuss cane growers' issues
articles.blurb: CM D.K. Shivakumar said he sought PM Narendra Modi’s appointment for an all-party delegation on cane and drought, appealed to farmers to end protests, and said State financial contribution to support price could be discussed.

articles.headline: Beyond religiosity (Opinion)
articles.blurb: The editorial says 19 deaths in Saturday’s Kolkata Girish Park pandal stampede could have been avoided with better crowd regulation, noting narrow lanes, rain-driven surges, organisers’ collapse warnings and mainly temporary home guards instead of experienced police.

articles.headline: Treacherous waters (Opinion)
articles.blurb: It links unsafe Ganga-Bihar boat crossings—including 13 children drowned in Vaishali on October 13 on an overloaded night trip—to weak enforcement of ferry rules and the lack of safer public transport for disadvantaged communities.

articles.headline: Developing minds in a digital world, a changing India (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Derick H. Lindquist argues constant digital and AI exposure during brain development demands device-free time, productive struggle in schools, and scrutiny of platforms targeting India’s ~65 crore under-25 population.

articles.headline: A case for joining the global carbon coalition (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Vaibhav Chaturvedi and Catherine Wolfram urge India to join the Open Coalition on Compliance Carbon Markets now that its Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is live, to shape interoperability rules and prepare for CBAM-style border measures.

articles.headline: Calm communication (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Letter writer K. Chidanand Kumar proposes trained ‘Voice of Calm’ announcers, marked exits, crowd limits and drills at pandals so emergencies do not trigger panic.

articles.headline: Revamp functioning of Parliament (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Atharva Deshmukh and Mehul Chhabra warn that expanding the Lok Sabha to 850 without more sitting days or protected Question Hour and Zero Hour time will dilute MPs’ floor voice despite delimitation easing voter loads.

articles.headline: On Abdullah's promise of Statehood (Opinion)
articles.blurb: Peerzada Ashiq writes that Omar Abdullah’s 2024 NC victory has not secured J&K Statehood, L-G control over police and bureaucracy has enervated his government, and he is hardening stance via Assembly resolutions and Jantar Mantar protest.

articles.headline: Analysing female labour of the North East States and UTs
articles.blurb: PLFS 2025 data show rural female LFPR rose from 33% to 45.9% since 2019-20, with Arunachal Pradesh’s average annual rural gain at 8.28 percentage points versus India’s 2.58, while Delhi and Lakshadweep saw declines.

articles.headline: Families mourn young lives lost in Durga Puja stampede
articles.blurb: Bereaved families queued at a Kolkata mortuary on Sunday after Saturday’s stampede killed 19, including 13 females and victims as young as seven; police listed seven dead from North 24 Parganas and CM Suvendu Adhikari promised dignified handover of bodies.

articles.headline: Shots fired at Tiger Shroff's car; 2 hurt, suspect detained
articles.blurb: Gunmen fired on Tiger Shroff’s car in Juhu around 7 p.m. on Sunday; driver Firdaus and bystander Chauhan were injured, one suspect was detained, and CM Devendra Fadnavis ordered a swift probe amid gang-claim social media posts.

articles.headline: CISF to overhaul its administrative structure
articles.blurb: MHA-approved CISF reorganisation effective November 1 creates sector-specific commands including Power, Coal, Steel, Petroleum & Natural Gas and East/West Coast Port sectors, plus GBMM & MRTS in Delhi, to match expanded critical-infrastructure duties.

articles.headline: SC bars mid-term fee hike in professional courses
articles.blurb: The Supreme Court ruled students in multi-year professional programmes must know total fee liability upfront; mid-stream hikes are impermissible except in extraordinary conditions, citing NSSO data that professional fees are 711% above general programmes.

articles.headline: Two held in Haryana over attack on bus bound for J&K
articles.blurb: Two men were arrested after stones and bricks damaged a Delhi–Srinagar sleeper bus near Karnal on Saturday night, injuring an elderly Kashmiri passenger; CM Nayab Singh Saini said the FIR followed a parking dispute between drivers.

articles.headline: Kuki organisation announces 'total shutdown' of highway in Manipur after attacks
articles.blurb: WCKCSO called a four-day NH-202 shutdown from October 18 after Kamjong village attacks that killed one Kuki and torched about 15 houses; Kamjong SP Tholu Rocky was replaced by Jay Barange amid Naga-Kuki blame exchanges.

articles.headline: Many held as youth groups attempt Jantar Mantar march
articles.blurb: NSUI’s ‘Ungli Toh Uthegi’ march from Raisina Road and other groups’ attempts to reach Jantar Mantar on Sunday demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and scrapping of SIR were stopped and many detained within metres.

articles.headline: Modi, Shah, CEC will face justice and pay the price for vote theft, says Rahul
articles.blurb: At Margao, Rahul Gandhi alleged Modi planned ‘vote theft’, Shah operationalised it and CEC Kumar implemented SIR, urged a 2027 Congress majority in Goa, and claimed evidence of malpractice in multiple States.

articles.headline: Audit in 2 Delhi booths finds over 100 voters wrongly marked absent, shifted, dead
articles.blurb: A seven-day Batla House Jan Sunwai audit of booths 61 and 65 in Okhla found 100-plus voters wrongly in ASDD lists; retired professor Faiyaz Ahmed, 74, was marked untraceable despite decades at the same address.

articles.headline: Drug-linked deaths: Oppn. steps up heat on AAP govt.
articles.blurb: Congress in-charge Sachin Pilot attacked the Punjab AAP government on drugs and law and order after anti-drug crusader Parvinder Singh Jhota’s October 13 killing; BJP said Amit Shah will visit Punjab on October 20.

articles.headline: Delhi's new protest sites face access, infrastructure, visibility hurdles
articles.blurb: After Jantar Mantar’s de-notification, visits to Ramlila Maidan, CBD Ground Shahdara and Burari Ground found booking costs, poor facilities, distance from central Delhi and competing events limiting their use as protest venues.

articles.headline: Conspiracy hatched by anti-India gangs: Rijiju
articles.blurb: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju alleged anti-India gangs and politicians instigated Delhi SIR protests like unrest in France and Bangladesh, insisted government change must come only via elections ‘not through Soros’, and criticised George Soros-linked groups.

articles.headline: Five killed as car rams State transport bus in Maharashtra
articles.blurb: Five Majalgaon residents including an 11-year-old died near Shindewadi Cross on the Khamgaon–Pandharpur NH on Sunday when their car hit an MSRTC bus after swerving for potholes; locals blockaded the road citing poor highway maintenance.

articles.headline: Assam SIT to approach SC against bail in Zubeen case
articles.blurb: Assam Police SIT chief Munna Prasad Gupta said the team will move the Supreme Court against bail to Amritprabha Mahanta and Sandipan Garg in the Zubeen Garg death case granted by Gauhati High Court on October 9 and 16.

articles.headline: Oil firms bar ethanol from sugar for blending in fuel
articles.blurb: OMCs’ October 16 tender for 2026-27 seeks about 11 billion litres of ethanol for 20% blending but bars sugar-cane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses per government directions, cutting maize incentive to ₹68.86 a litre from ₹71.86.

articles.headline: Handle perishables only in controlled conditions: FSSAI
articles.blurb: FSSAI advised food business operators to store and transport khoa, paneer, meat and fish under controlled temperatures and told State commissioners and Railways to enforce Schedule 4 hygiene rules against spoilage and cross-contamination.

articles.headline: Study flags impact of Internet use on children
articles.blurb: An ICSSR-supported 2025 study of 2,000 children aged 9–14 found 97.6% access the Internet from home, with anxiety, sleep issues and mood changes most reported; nearly 47% admitted talking to strangers online in six months.

articles.headline: IIT-B student death: police detain parents, demolish protest site
articles.blurb: Mumbai Police detained Sahil Wakode’s parents and 16 students and demolished a month-long IIT-Bombay protest site on Sunday demanding arrest of Professor Suryanarayana Doola named in the suicide FIR.

articles.headline: Sikkim parties slam Gautam's appointment as Governor
articles.blurb: Sikkim Congress and SDF demanded recall of new Governor Dushyant Kumar Gautam until the CBI completes the Ankita Bhandari murder probe; Bhandari, 19, was killed at a Uttarakhand resort on September 18, 2022.

articles.headline: What if a cheque bounces?
articles.blurb: Legal column explains Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act penalties up to two years’ imprisonment and twice the cheque amount for dishonour after demand notice timelines, with ₹50,000 example and three-year civil recovery limits.

articles.headline: Your claim may be cashless but not costless
articles.blurb: Insurance column warns cashless hospitalisation still leaves co-pays, exclusions, room-rent caps and non-covered consumables—the hospital bill and admissible claim are not the same.

articles.headline: Finances for disabled
articles.blurb: Column urges persons with disabilities to use equity SIPs, Section 80U deductions of ₹75,000 or ₹1.25 lakh, health cover and term insurance for caregivers, citing 11–13% healthcare inflation versus 5–6% consumer inflation.

articles.headline: India asks its nationals to follow safety directives in Saudi Arabia
articles.blurb: The Indian Embassy in Riyadh on Sunday asked nationals to follow Saudi National Early Warning Platform directives amid heightened security after Houthi strikes.

articles.headline: Trump endorses ally Netanyahu ahead of Israel's tight election
articles.blurb: Donald Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu before Israel’s October 27 parliamentary election; Netanyahu said re-election would let them work to ‘eliminate the Iranian threat’.

articles.headline: Four killed and dozens injured in fire at military base in Canada
articles.blurb: PM Mark Carney said four Canadian Forces members died and dozens were seriously injured in Sunday’s fire at CFB Wainwright, Alberta, during training.

articles.headline: Trump to take up to 60 days to weigh Russia sanctions, says Rubio
articles.blurb: After waiving Russia sanctions, Donald Trump has not finalised a decision; Secretary of State Marco Rubio said up to 60 days will be used to assess economic impact.

articles.headline: French police arrest 1,800 after violent clashes, looting mar protests
articles.blurb: At least 1,800 were arrested after masked groups looted shops and burned Limoges City Hall during nationwide cost-of-living protests drawing 5.5–8 lakh people; over 500 security personnel were injured.

articles.headline: Akhlaghi warns of 'enormous damage' if U.S. attacks Iran
articles.blurb: New Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi after Parliament’s confidence vote said a U.S. attack would inflict enormous damage on Washington and the region.

articles.headline: 'Drove away Chinese vessels involved in maritime harassment'
articles.blurb: Taiwan’s coast guard said it drove away 16 Chinese coast guard, research and fishing vessels in coordinated operations around Taiwan and Pratas, with some entering restricted waters.

articles.headline: Fire at St. Petersburg oil refineries after Kyiv launches drones
articles.blurb: Ukraine’s 1,000-plus drone attack killed one and wounded five in St. Petersburg, igniting the oil terminal and Ruchi depot; Russia said it destroyed 1,015 drones while Zaporizhzhia also came under fire.

articles.headline: Vance defends 'indentured servants' remark on H-1B workers, admits 'imperfect rhetoric'
articles.blurb: U.S. Vice-President J.D. Vance told a CBS town hall his H-1B ‘indentured servants’ comment targeted the visa system, not holders; India had called the term deeply offensive.

articles.headline: DP World extends partnership with India Championship till 2035
articles.blurb: DP World will partner the DP World India Championship through 2035, keeping the event on the Race to Dubai, CEO Yuvraj Narayan citing India as a key global trade market.

articles.headline: Talwar emerges the 2026 DP World PGTI Order of Merit winner
articles.blurb: Saptak Talwar won the 2026 DP World PGTI Order of Merit with one victory and eight top-10 finishes after splitting time between PGTI and HotelPlanner Tour.

articles.headline: Boland strikes twice on rain-hit opening day of second Test
articles.blurb: Scott Boland took two wickets in two balls as rain limited the Gqeberha second Test to 12.2 overs with South Africa 20 for two after Australia won the toss.

articles.headline: Salman, Afridi shine as Pakistan defeats Sri Lanka in opener
articles.blurb: Salman Agha’s 107 and Shaheen Afridi’s 3/55 helped Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 37 runs in Rawalpindi: 305 vs 268 in the ODI tri-series opener.

articles.headline: Chacarra holds his own, clinches the title in style
articles.blurb: Eugenio Chacarra won the DP World India Championship by two shots at Delhi Golf Club with a final 70 after a third-round 63, leading the Race to Dubai; Daniel Hillier was second and Rory McIlroy tied-42.

articles.headline: Chacarra dedicates the triumph to his late grandfather
articles.blurb: Chacarra dedicated his Delhi win to grandfather Francisco, who died 10 days earlier, after overcoming neck pain and a broken toe; it is his fourth DP World Tour title.

articles.headline: Shafali, Smriti power India to series win
articles.blurb: Shafali Verma’s 25-ball 55 and Smriti Mandhana’s 47 not out chased 103 in 8.5 overs as India beat Zimbabwe by nine wickets in Raipur for a 2-0 T20I series lead; third match on October 20.

articles.headline: Marathas prove Mighty
articles.blurb: Mighty Marathas beat Kakatiya Knights 6-2 in the Archery Premier League Season 2 final at Hyderabad People’s Plaza as Dhiraj Bommadevara’s 79 in the last set sealed the title.

articles.headline: Are Bhuvneshwar, Dhir the missing pieces?
articles.blurb: India conceded 220-plus T20 totals five times in 2025 including 2-2 vs West Indies; Shreyas Iyer cited execution gaps while the piece notes Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return and Naman Dhir’s form ahead of New Zealand.

articles.headline: Arsenal leaves it late to get past Forest
articles.blurb: Noni Madueke’s 80th-minute goal gave Arsenal a 1-0 Premier League win at Nottingham Forest; select results also included Barcelona’s 5-2 LaLiga win over Betis and Bayern’s 6-1 over Leipzig.

articles.headline: India's Para Asiad contingent displays 5,000-year heritage
articles.blurb: Over 100 Indian athletes at the Para Asian Games opening wore blazers with Indus Valley motifs; India’s 281-member contingent includes 168 athletes in 11 disciplines led by Simran Sharma and Pramod Bhagat.

articles.headline: Chwalinska overcomes Kartal, wins maiden WTA crown
articles.blurb: Maja Chwalinska beat Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in 2:43 to win the Wuhan Open, her first WTA title, projected to reach world No. 11.

articles.headline: Manvanth's gutsy knock lifts Karnataka on day one
articles.blurb: Manvanth Kumar’s unbeaten 86 from No. 9 lifted Karnataka to 281/8 vs Saurashtra at Alur on Ranji day one, sharing 87 with Abhilash Shetty after Jaydev Unadkat and Parth Bhut took three wickets each.

articles.headline: RANJI TROPHY SCORES — ROUND 2, DAY 1
articles.blurb: Round-two day-one highlights included Delhi 381/4 (Priyansh Arya 199), Punjab 269/4 (Uday Saharan 106 batting), UP 202 (Rinku Singh 118 not out) and Karnataka 281/8 vs Saurashtra across elite and plate groups.

articles.headline: Experienced Bhuvneshwar a shoo-in for T20Is: Shastri
articles.blurb: Ravi Shastri called Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s T20I recall a ‘no-brainer’ after IPL form and said India’s New Zealand tour from October 22 will test Shubman Gill’s captaincy across five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests.

articles.headline: Jaskaran and Chandermohan enter bronze medal bouts at u-23 Worlds
articles.blurb: At Las Vegas u-23 worlds, Jaskaran Singh (65kg) and Chandermohan (79kg) reached bronze bouts while Rohit (57kg) and Shivam (97kg) stayed alive via repechage.

articles.headline: Lokesh clinches u-17 crown in Malaysia junior squash
articles.blurb: India’s Lokesh Subramani beat Muhammad Ifwat Zulkifli 11-6, 11-2, 11-8 in Kuala Lumpur to win the Malaysia junior open boys’ under-17 title.

articles.headline: EBFC downs Churchill; NEUFC beats KBFC
articles.blurb: East Bengal beat Churchill Brothers 4-0 in Margao with Dani Ramirez scoring twice; NorthEast United beat Kerala Blasters 4-1 in Guwahati with Ajaraie scoring twice.

articles.headline: Fokina rallies to get past Jodar, lifts Shanghai Masters title
articles.blurb: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina beat Rafael Jodar 1-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 for his first ATP Masters 1000 title in Shanghai.

articles.headline: Bopanna advises me to believe in myself, says Khushi
articles.blurb: 13-year-old Khushi Kadian won Fenesta Open u-16 singles, doubles and u-14 singles in New Delhi, training at Rohan Bopanna Academy in Bengaluru ahead of ITF events.

articles.headline: Krish, Rivaan, Arshi and Ayansh reign supreme
articles.blurb: Krish Gupta, Rivaan Dev Preetham, Arshi Gupta and Ayansh Patil clinched MECO FMSCI National Karting titles in Bengaluru on Sunday despite not winning the final round-six races.

articles.headline: Prahas slams century for RBNCC 'B'
articles.blurb: Prahas S. Nairy’s 160 powered RBNCC ‘B’ to 301 vs The Mysore Gymkhana’s 179 in a drawn KSCA Mysore zone first-division match at SJCE; KSCA also felicitated Shreyas Gopal for 100 first-class matches.

articles.headline: India's scheduling SNAFU — how much is too much?
articles.blurb: R. Kaushik notes Shreyas Iyer’s India played 21 T20Is in 114 days across five countries before flying to New Zealand with one full practice session, citing Morne Morkel on mental fatigue and Tilak Varma saying pros cannot offer excuses.

articles.headline: Two-face molecule could help make IBD treatments more effective
articles.blurb: NII research in PNAS finds RelB paradoxically drives IL-23 sentinel cells in gut lymphoid tissue while suppressing regulatory T-cells in lymph nodes, complicating IBD drugs that block IL-23.

articles.headline: Satellite radiation: blocking views
articles.blurb: SNIFFLES monitoring with Mopra and ATCA found Starlink, OneWeb and Guowang emissions—including signals up to 100-billion-times brighter than astronomical sources—interfering with radio astronomy across intended, unwanted and unintended categories.

articles.headline: Separation of powers and CJI's refusal
articles.blurb: Explainer: CJI Surya Kant declined an October 12 meeting with Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge on CEC Gyanesh Kumar and SIR arrests, citing separation of powers and pending litigation, advising writ remedies instead; Gandhi subsequently filed a petition.

articles.headline: After a decade of disruption, Pattanam needs a renewed vision
articles.blurb: P.J. Cherian argues excavations at Pattanam (300 BCE–300 CE) proved a major Indian Ocean node but research paused from 2016–2026; reviving multidisciplinary work and a Pattanam Heritage Authority could restore global archaeology-education ties.
